Project overview / Priority tables

County diabetes outreach priority tables

CDC PLACES County Data, 2025 release (diagnosed diabetes among adults, BRFSS 2023), Census Bureau Vintage 2023 adult population estimates and ACS 2020-2024 poverty estimates. Kentucky and Pennsylvania have no diagnosed-diabetes estimates in this release and are not listed. Run a944852459ca.

Each rule ranks the same counties differently. Core counties are selected wherever every county's value falls within the bounds used for that rule (the published PLACES 95% limits and, for estimated burden, scenario bounds that also span the adult population range). Boundary counties are selected for some values within the bounds. For high-poverty prevalence, eligibility also spans the ACS 95% poverty bounds. A county whose upper bound reaches 20% can be boundary, and only a county whose lower bound reaches 20% can be core. These labels describe the published estimates and are not probabilities. All values below were computed by the analysis pipeline. The filters only choose which rows to show.

County table

Ranks are competition ranks on the full national frame (or the full state) and ties share a rank. High-poverty prevalence ranks counties whose poverty estimate is at least 20%. Counties with an estimate below 20% but an upper 95% bound of 20% or more have no point rank (shown as not eligible at estimate) but can be boundary, and counties whose bounds straddle 20% cannot be core. Poverty is ACS 2020-2024 percent below the poverty level with 95% bounds.

Definitions

  • Prevalence: crude percentage of adults aged 18 and older reporting diagnosed diabetes (PLACES model-based estimate).
  • Estimated burden: prevalence times the adult population. Bounds combine the PLACES interval with the Vintage 2023 estimate and the ACS 2020-2024 95% range for adults. They are scenario bounds, not a confidence interval.
  • High-poverty prevalence: prevalence ranked among counties where at least 20% of people are below the poverty level. Counties whose poverty bounds straddle 20% can be boundary but not core.
  • States with 5 or fewer counties (District of Columbia, Delaware, Hawaii, Rhode Island): in the within-state view all units are listed and none is selected.
  • Best to worst rank: the best and worst rank a county can take when every county's value stays within its bounds.
